Risk Description: The planned React client and Go API may not integrate against the same request, response, error, and authorization contract.
Cause: No frontend or backend source is present; the OpenAPI file is a design artifact, and UI/API work has separate owners.
Potential Consequence: Broken workflows, rework, late integration, or frontend assumptions that bypass required server behavior.
Prevention: Agree and version API schemas, examples, error semantics, and role behavior before implementation; review contract changes with both owners.
Detection Method: Run contract checks and end-to-end smoke tests against the candidate build; compare observed responses to OpenAPI and UI handling.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Pause affected integration, agree a single contract change, update consumers and tests together, and rerun impacted workflows.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Frontend and backend produce incompatible payloads, errors, endpoints, or assumptions about authorization.
Related Requirement or Component: OpenAPI contract; React/Go integration; FR-RBAC-001; NFR-SEC-002

Risk Description: Persistent records may violate relationship, booking-overlap, exact-value, or transaction invariants.
Cause: No database schema or migration exists yet; concurrent booking and atomic audit behavior are design requirements only.
Potential Consequence: Duplicate or orphaned records, overlapping bookings, lost updates, incorrect reports, or partial business/audit writes.
Prevention: Design reviewed migrations, foreign keys, unique and exclusion constraints, transaction boundaries, and recovery behavior before data-bearing workflows ship.
Detection Method: Run disposable PostgreSQL integration/concurrency tests, constraint checks, transaction fault injection, and API-versus-stored-state comparisons.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Stop affected writes, preserve evidence, restore from a verified backup if needed, reconcile data with an approved repair, and block release until integrity tests pass.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Migration or constraint is missing; concurrent test creates two overlapping bookings; failure leaves partial state.
Related Requirement or Component: PostgreSQL design; FR-APPT-002; FR-CLIENT-002; FR-DEAL-001; NFR-DATA-001; NFR-AUD-001

Risk Description: The implemented API may diverge from the OpenAPI contract or provide inconsistent errors and precondition behavior.
Cause: OpenAPI is not backed by an application; contract is version 0.1.0-design and later changes may not be propagated to implementation/tests.
Potential Consequence: Clients cannot reliably handle responses; unauthorized or stale writes may be accepted; consumer breakage and rework.
Prevention: Treat reviewed OpenAPI as versioned interface; update examples and implementation together; review breaking changes and generated/tested schemas.
Detection Method: Run static validator plus live contract tests for status, headers, schemas, error shapes, ETags, idempotency, and pagination.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Restore compatibility or version the contract, coordinate client update, and defer release of incompatible changes.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Live endpoint missing, shape/header differs from schema, or contract validator fails.
Related Requirement or Component: api/openapi.yaml; 27 proposed operations; NFR-MAINT-001; NFR-REL-001; NFR-SEC-002

Risk Description: Unhandled application or dependency errors may produce partial operations, unsafe error responses, or an unavailable workflow.
Cause: No runtime error-handling implementation or test environment is available to verify the proposed RFC 9457 responses and failure paths.
Potential Consequence: Data corruption, secret/stack disclosure, user confusion, or service outage.
Prevention: Define error mapping and transaction boundaries; avoid success-shaped fallbacks; use bounded timeouts and fail-safe defaults with explicit errors.
Detection Method: Exercise malformed input, database/audit/provider faults, and unexpected errors; inspect response bodies, logs, and persisted state.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Disable the failing integration or write path, return a safe explicit error, restore service/data from verified recovery procedures, and retest before enabling.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Unmapped error, panic/crash, stack trace or sensitive value in response/log, or mutation succeeds despite failed audit.
Related Requirement or Component: Backend transport and service error handling; NFR-SEC-002; NFR-REL-002

Risk Description: A future deployment may fail or run with unsafe configuration because startup, environment, secrets, migration, TLS, and backup procedures are not implemented or specified fully.
Cause: No deployment manifests, executable startup instructions, migration runner, or operational test environment are present.
Potential Consequence: Unavailable or misconfigured service, loss of data, exposed credentials, or inability to restore after failure.
Prevention: Create a reviewed deployment/runbook, validate required configuration at startup, keep secrets out of source control, apply reviewed migrations, and test backups/restores in non-production.
Detection Method: Use clean-environment startup and configuration tests; inspect deployment logs and conduct a scheduled restore drill once an environment exists.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Roll back to last known-good build/configuration, disable unsafe ingress, rotate exposed secrets, and restore from verified backup.
Trigger or Warning Sign: A clean deployment requires undocumented manual steps, missing environment variables are silently defaulted, or a restore has not been demonstrated.
Related Requirement or Component: Deployment and operations; README; NFR-REL-002; NFR-SEC-001

Risk Description: API and database latency may exceed user expectations or the proposed non-AI response-time goal under realistic load.
Cause: No application or benchmark exists; 20 concurrent users and 1,000 synthetic clients with p95 below 500 ms is a proposed target only.
Potential Consequence: Slow workflows, timeouts, retries, user abandonment, or cascading resource pressure.
Prevention: Keep queries bounded/indexed and response sizes limited; approve a representative workload and target before performance tuning.
Detection Method: Run repeatable non-AI load tests on documented hardware; report p50/p95/p99, errors, timeouts, and database latency separately.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Profile the constrained component, reduce workload/query cost or revise capacity/design with stakeholder approval; do not claim target compliance without rerun evidence.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Measured p95 exceeds approved target, database waits grow, or timeout/retry rates rise under agreed load.
Related Requirement or Component: NFR-PERF-001; reporting and CRM endpoints; proposed 500 ms target

Risk Description: Critical regressions may reach review or demonstration because no executable application tests exist in the repository.
Cause: Current automated check validates the OpenAPI document only; PD-15 runtime cases are planned, not executed.
Potential Consequence: Authentication, authorization, data integrity, and core workflows remain unverified and defects escape detection.
Prevention: Require implementation owners to add unit, integration, API, database, and UI tests for critical paths; prioritize P0 test cases and synthetic fixtures.
Detection Method: Track linked test execution by requirement/build; run regression, role matrix, concurrency, and fault tests in CI or documented local runs.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Block release/demo claims for unverified critical behavior; reduce scope to verifiable functionality and schedule implementation/test work.
Trigger or Warning Sign: New source or endpoint is delivered without linked executable tests; runtime cases remain Not Run near a release decision.
Related Requirement or Component: PD-15 suite; 36 runtime cases Not Run at PD-15 baseline; all FR/NFR acceptance

Risk Description: Unpinned or unreviewed runtime dependencies may introduce incompatible behavior, supply-chain exposure, or unavailable services.
Cause: Go, React, PostgreSQL deployment versions, AI provider, and most runtime dependencies have not been selected or implemented in the baseline.
Potential Consequence: Build/release failure, vulnerabilities, license or compatibility issues, provider outage, or unplanned migration work.
Risk Owner: Backend Developer; Frontend Developer; AI Integration Owner
Prevention: Select supported versions, commit lockfiles, review dependency provenance/licenses/advisories, minimize dependency scope, and define provider abstraction/fallback.
Detection Method: Run dependency inventory and vulnerability/advisory review on locked dependencies; monitor build reproducibility and provider health.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Pin/upgrade or replace affected dependency after compatibility tests; disable optional provider-dependent features while preserving manual CRM paths.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Unreproducible build, unreviewed package/provider addition, advisory affecting deployed dependency, or provider terms change.
Related Requirement or Component: Dependency management; Go/React/PostgreSQL stack; AI provider adapter

Risk Description: The proposed assistant may return fabricated, incomplete, or incorrect client summaries or task/appointment fields.
Cause: Generative output is probabilistic and the model/provider is not selected; no evaluation corpus or observed output exists.
Potential Consequence: Users may act on incorrect CRM information, schedule errors, or create inaccurate work records.
Prevention: Use authorized bounded retrieval, source handles, schema/business validation, explicit clarification for ambiguity, and human review before writes; keep manual forms available.
Detection Method: Evaluate frozen synthetic held-out cases using case exactness, field-level precision/recall/F1, grounding checks, and human-reviewed reference answers.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Suppress unsupported claims/proposals, show verified source records or a clear fallback, correct affected records, and suspend the failing intent pending retest.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Mismatch between model answer and retrieved source, repeated missing/wrong slots, or user correction reports.
Related Requirement or Component: Proposed AI intents only; FR-AI-001; FR-AI-002; PD-16 AI evaluation plan

Risk Description: User text or retrieved content may attempt prompt injection that induces broader retrieval, disclosure, tool use, or unsafe output.
Cause: Any future natural-language input is untrusted; no AI implementation or adversarial test results exist.
Potential Consequence: Sensitive information disclosure, unauthorized data access, or unsafe instructions presented as trusted output.
Prevention: Treat prompts and retrieved text as data; expose only an allowlisted intent interface and bounded authorized context; prohibit generic SQL, shell, arbitrary URL, or tool authority.
Detection Method: Run synthetic adversarial prompt suites and inspect actual retrieval/tool calls, provider payloads, response rendering, and security logs.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Disable the affected AI intent/provider route, preserve sanitized evidence, notify security owner, and resume only after policy/schema correction and regression tests.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Model attempts an unapproved tool/intent, retrieves an unauthorized record, or follows instructions embedded in user/context text.
Related Requirement or Component: AI trust boundary; FR-AI-001; FR-AI-002; NFR-PRIV-001; NFR-SEC-003

Risk Description: An AI-generated proposal could cause a business mutation without valid, current, actor-bound human confirmation.
Cause: Proposal lifecycle and confirmation endpoint/UI are design requirements but are not implemented or available in OpenAPI.
Potential Consequence: Unauthorized, altered, replayed, or stale task/appointment is committed; loss of user control and auditability.
Prevention: Keep model output non-executable; bind immutable proposal to actor, arguments, expiry, and versions; require explicit confirmation and recheck permissions/state in the normal transaction.
Detection Method: Test no-write-before-confirm, altered args, other actor, expiry, permission change, replay, concurrency, and audit atomicity using disposable records.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Immediately disable AI write proposals; revoke outstanding proposals; inspect/repair affected test data; require security review and full regression before re-enable.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Any business row changes before confirmation, mismatched proposal is accepted, or duplicate confirmation creates multiple records.
Related Requirement or Component: FR-AI-003; FR-AI-004; NFR-AUD-001; AI proposal lifecycle

Risk Description: An external AI provider may be unavailable, rate-limited, slow, or change service behavior.
Cause: Provider/model is unselected and externally operated; no provider service-level or outage evidence exists.
Potential Consequence: Assistant becomes unavailable, manual tasks are delayed, or user-facing errors/retries consume resources.
Prevention: Keep AI optional, set bounded timeouts and retry limits, monitor provider outcomes, avoid coupling manual CRM routes to provider health, and document approved provider fallback.
Detection Method: Use mock-provider timeout/429/5xx tests; monitor latency, error rates, and provider/version changes after controlled deployment.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Return explicit AI-unavailable state and route users to manual forms; disable provider integration until recovery is confirmed.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Timeout, 429/5xx increase, provider model/terms change, or manual path is blocked by AI outage.
Related Requirement or Component: FR-AI-004; NFR-REL-002; proposed external provider adapter

Risk Description: Retries of an AI confirmation or uncertain create request may produce duplicate side effects.
Cause: Network timeouts and retries are possible; proposal consumption and endpoint idempotency are not implemented for AI operations.
Potential Consequence: Duplicate tasks/appointments, double audit events, confusing user state, or inconsistent retries.
Prevention: Define confirmation replay semantics, consume proposals atomically, use scoped idempotency for permitted creates, and return a stable outcome for the same operation.
Detection Method: Inject lost responses and repeat sequential/concurrent confirmations; compare resource and audit counts in a disposable database.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Stop automatic retries, reconcile the intended record with the user, deduplicate only through an approved repair, and disable affected action until corrected.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Repeated confirmation or retry yields more than one mutation, or client cannot tell whether first attempt committed.
Related Requirement or Component: FR-AI-003; NFR-REL-001; NFR-DATA-001

Risk Description: Equivalent requests may produce inconsistent intents or fields across model versions or repeated runs.
Cause: Provider/model selection, decoding parameters, prompt versioning, and output regression protocol are not established.
Potential Consequence: Unpredictable user experience, unstable acceptance results, or regressions after provider changes.
Prevention: Pin and record provider/model and prompt/schema versions; use deterministic settings where supported; keep outputs constrained and independently validate all candidates.
Detection Method: Repeat fixed corpus across runs and version upgrades; report per-intent exactness, field error categories, and variance.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Roll back model/prompt configuration, narrow or disable failing intents, and rerun the held-out regression suite before restoring.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Provider silently changes version, repeated fixed prompts yield materially different structured fields, or quality metrics regress.
Related Requirement or Component: FR-AI-002; NFR-MAINT-001; PD-16 evaluation controls

Risk Description: Authentication and server-side role/ownership enforcement may be absent or incorrectly implemented when runtime endpoints are built.
Cause: Authentication, session revocation, RBAC, and ownership checks exist only in design/API annotations; no application middleware or handlers are present.
Potential Consequence: Account compromise, unauthorized reads/writes, or privileged account changes.
Prevention: Implement middleware and service-level policy from validated session identity; use reviewed password/session storage and route/field matrix; do not trust browser or model authority.
Detection Method: Run direct API tests for unauthenticated, invalid/expired/revoked sessions, every role, forbidden fields, and cross-user access; review persisted state after denial.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Disable affected routes, revoke compromised sessions/credentials, assess exposure, repair authorization and data, and require independent retest before release.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Protected route is reachable without valid session; client-supplied role changes outcome; denial still mutates state.
Related Requirement or Component: FR-AUTH-001–004; FR-RBAC-001–005; NFR-SEC-001; NFR-SEC-004

Risk Description: Employee-scoped deals, tasks, appointments, or related client context may leak across users through lookup, pagination, reports, errors, or AI retrieval.
Cause: Ownership filtering and shared-client boundary are architectural requirements but not implemented; client access does not grant access to related employee records.
Potential Consequence: Disclosure of business/contact data, privacy harm, or loss of trust.
Risk Owner: Backend Developer; Security Owner; AI Integration Owner
Prevention: Apply ownership predicates before counts/order/pagination and at every service/read path; explicitly separate shared client fields from owned records; enforce the same rules in AI retrieval.
Detection Method: Cross-user list/item/report/API tests; compare response/errors for inaccessible vs missing IDs; inspect AI retrieval and provider payloads using synthetic canaries.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Disable affected read/report/AI features, restrict access, preserve audit evidence, assess potentially exposed data, and fix scope filters before re-enable.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Cross-user ID appears in list/search/report/context, or error reveals protected fields/existence contrary to contract.
Related Requirement or Component: FR-RBAC-002; FR-RBAC-004; FR-REPORT-001; FR-AI-001; NFR-PRIV-001

Risk Description: Credentials, bearer tokens, personal data, or conversation content may be exposed through storage, URLs, logs, errors, screenshots, or source control.
Cause: Security logging and secret-handling controls are specified but no implementation/deployment configuration has been inspected; provider is unselected.
Potential Consequence: Account takeover, unauthorized disclosure, incident response burden, or accidental publication of sensitive information.
Prevention: Keep secrets in approved secret storage; hash stored session tokens/passwords; restrict logs and redact payloads; use HTTPS outside local development; use synthetic data in demos and evidence.
Detection Method: Search repository and sanitized logs for canary secrets; review headers, storage, URLs, crash/error output, and access controls; run secret scanning when implementation exists.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Rotate exposed credentials, revoke tokens, restrict/delete exposed evidence under policy, assess incident scope, notify responsible parties as required, and remediate before release.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Canary secret appears in Git, logs, URL, response, browser persistent storage, or shared screenshot.
Related Requirement or Component: FR-AUTH-001–003; NFR-SEC-001; NFR-SEC-002; NFR-AUD-001

Risk Description: Personal/contact data may be sent to an external AI service without adequate minimization, processing review, or retention decisions.
Cause: The AI provider/model and its processing terms are not selected; proposed intent retrieval has not been implemented or reviewed in deployment context.
Potential Consequence: Unapproved third-party disclosure, privacy-policy breach, retention beyond project expectations, or inability to delete data.
Prevention: Use synthetic records for development; default to minimum fields; exclude credentials, auth/audit data, and unnecessary contact fields; approve provider retention/region/training/deletion terms before real data.
Detection Method: Capture and review outbound payloads with synthetic canaries; verify provider configuration and documented privacy review before enabling real-data use.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Disable provider/real-data path, rotate any exposed secret if applicable, follow approved incident/privacy process, and resume only after review and technical controls pass.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Provider unreviewed or configured for training/retention, or outbound payload contains unnecessary personal/secret fields.
Related Requirement or Component: NFR-PRIV-001; FR-AI-001; proposed AI provider adapter

Risk Description: Public API routes or deployment headers may be exposed without intended authentication, transport, body limits, CORS, or safe error controls.
Cause: The OpenAPI contract has security declarations and proposed local HTTP URL, but no deployed server, TLS, ingress, CORS, or middleware configuration exists.
Potential Consequence: Unauthorized operations, interception, injection/availability issues, or sensitive error disclosure.
Risk Owner: Security Owner; Deployment/Operations Owner; Backend Developer
Prevention: Review every route's auth exception and role policy; require TLS outside local development, configured CORS origins, size/time limits, safe errors, and explicit ingress rules.
Detection Method: Run route inventory and direct HTTP checks from allowed/unallowed origins; verify TLS, headers, body boundary, and error redaction in staging.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Remove public ingress or disable affected endpoint, correct gateway/application configuration, and retest route matrix before restoring access.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Unexpected unauthenticated route, wildcard origin, plaintext external transport, oversized-body acceptance, or stack trace returned.
Related Requirement or Component: api/openapi.yaml; NFR-SEC-002; NFR-SEC-003; NFR-SEC-004

Risk Description: Requirements, test cases, verification plan, and project documentation may describe different baselines or acceptance behavior.
Cause: PD-13, PD-14, PD-15, and PD-16 artifacts are on separately pushed, unmerged branches; downstream plans pin upstream commit IDs.
Potential Consequence: Conflicting acceptance criteria, duplicate work, invalid traceability, or review of a package that cannot be reproduced from one branch.
Prevention: Review and merge task artifacts in dependency order; record baseline commits and reconcile changed IDs/contracts before integrating downstream documents.
Detection Method: Compare requirement and test IDs across branch/commit references; check PR diffs and trace links before a release baseline is declared.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Freeze evaluation against one explicitly versioned baseline; amend dependent docs/tests in corrective commits after upstream changes.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Referenced file absent from main, source commit changes, or requirement/test ID mismatch after upstream review.
Related Requirement or Component: PD-13/PD-14/PD-15/PD-16 branch integration; traceability baseline

Risk Description: Unresolved assumptions may be treated as approved requirements or product decisions.
Cause: Requirements and architecture are proposed; shared-client visibility, rate limits, performance/accessibility targets, provider/privacy policy, and some operational choices need confirmation.
Potential Consequence: Rework, disputes about acceptance, unsafe assumptions, or evaluation against criteria stakeholders never accepted.
Prevention: Maintain a decision log with decision owner, options, rationale, date, and impact; mark proposed targets and unresolved policies explicitly; obtain approval before gating release.
Detection Method: Review open questions in PD-14 and verification plan at each milestone; verify approval evidence before declaring criterion satisfied.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Defer affected feature or use the safest bounded behavior; revise acceptance tests and communicate scope change after explicit decision.
Trigger or Warning Sign: A test expects unapproved behavior, target is presented as achieved/mandatory without sign-off, or role/privacy policy is disputed.
Related Requirement or Component: PD-14 open questions; NFR-PERF-001; NFR-USAB-003; NFR-PRIV-001; AI provider policy

Risk Description: Frontend/backend work may be delayed or require rework because interface decisions and dependency timing are not coordinated.
Cause: Repository assigns separate frontend and backend/AI responsibilities; no executable frontend prototype or backend is present and no integration schedule is recorded.
Potential Consequence: Late end-to-end integration, incomplete MVP flows, blocked QA, or incompatible implementations.
Risk Owner: Project Lead; Frontend Developer; Backend Developer
Prevention: Agree API/error/timezone/auth/confirmation contracts early; define integration checkpoints and demoable vertical slices; surface blockers without waiting for all modules.
Detection Method: Track agreed interface decisions, branch/PR dependencies, integrated build availability, and unresolved contract changes.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Prioritize a minimum vertical slice; negotiate scope or sequence with stakeholders; document deferred features rather than claiming completion.
Trigger or Warning Sign: Frontend has no API to integrate, backend contract changes after UI work, or integration checkpoint lacks a working build.
Related Requirement or Component: React/Go integration; PD-10 prototype dependency; API contract

Risk Description: Independent review or task ownership may be delayed if reviewer identity, availability, or cross-team assignment is not confirmed.
Cause: Repository notes reviewer usernames are pending verification and tasks depend on work owned by different contributors; actual availability is not recorded.
Potential Consequence: Unreviewed changes, delayed integration, unresolved defects, or incorrect attribution of work/approval.
Prevention: Confirm reviewer and owner assignments on the project board before review windows; do not infer availability or claim approval; preserve handoff notes and task dependencies.
Detection Method: Check PR reviewer requests, task-board assignment, response status, and unresolved review comments at agreed checkpoints.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Reassign only with team agreement; narrow or defer dependent work and report the block rather than bypassing independent review.
Trigger or Warning Sign: No verified reviewer/owner is assigned, review requests remain pending, or a dependent task cannot progress.
Related Requirement or Component: CONTRIBUTING.md ownership/review workflow; project board

Risk Description: There may be insufficient time or access to complete implementation, independent review, and meaningful user evaluation before project milestones.
Cause: No confirmed project schedule, prototype, participant recruitment, implementation plan, or evaluation environment appears in the inspected repository.
Potential Consequence: The project may end with design artifacts but no demonstrated system, or with unsupported product-value claims and incomplete QA.
Prevention: Confirm actual milestones and dependencies; prioritize implementation and verification of MVP/P0 requirements; reserve time for integration, defects, and evaluation; approve a reduced but explicit study scope if needed.
Detection Method: Track working build availability, completed P0 tests, outstanding dependencies, participant/evaluation readiness, and elapsed time against the confirmed project plan.
Contingency or Recovery Plan: Replan with stakeholder agreement; protect core demo and safety validation; mark unavailable evaluations as not performed and carry residual risks forward.
Trigger or Warning Sign: No runnable prototype/build by evaluation start, critical cases remain Not Run, or participant/data approvals are not ready.
Related Requirement or Component: Project schedule not evidenced; PD-16 evaluation phases; OBJ-02–OBJ-06
